newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah bounces back on offshore buying.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah bounces back on offshore buying.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah bounced back to 2,450/54 against the dollar at 0220 GMT on Monday after offshore players turned the market around with dollar unloading, dealers said.
They said offshore players seemed to be trying to cash out from the market after they drove the rupiah to a low of 2,469.0 on Monday morning.
"I think some feel that the rupiah is low enough for a buy back, reversing the market trend," one local bank dealer said.

But another local bank dealer said the rupiah buying initiative was started by some state banks which was followed through by offshore players, driving the rupiah to a high of 2,445 before operators bought some dollar back.
He said spot rates settled at around 2,450/54.0 at 0245 GMT but the overall market condition remained volatile.
One U.S. bank dealer said offshore operators continued to accumulate rupiah in the swap market, preparing themselves in case the central bank squeezed money market liquidity.
Six-month swaps were at around 120/130 points.
But money market dealers said there was no such indication because rupiah liquidity was abundant in the market, with overnight rates falling to 13.0 percent from 19.5 percent.
